ZERO_TWO_RIGHT.auc_direction_folded_grid_is: the same value with its direction folded away, which is what a fitted one-predictor logistic regression returns in sample; it cannot fall below 0.5, so for THAT number 0.5 is a floor and the shuffled level in the table below is what it has to beat

notes: The circled cell in each column is the LARGEST of the nine lengths tried for that band, chosen after the fact, so it runs larger than fresh ratings would; its corrected p and q are judged against the shuffled best-of-nine value. Other cells are uncorrected.
AUC 0.5, not 0, is no discrimination between high and low pain; an interval spanning 0.5 leaves the band unsettled, not empty.
The AUC map keeps direction: above 0.5 means higher power in high-pain reports, below means lower.
The 198 cells (9 lengths x 22 centres, 5 Hz wide, 1 Hz apart) overlap heavily and are not independent.

1543 single 3 s pieces above this contact's fixed historical ceiling (top 0.5% of its own record, per band) were dropped before averaging and replaced by the next clean piece, so every cell keeps its row's count.
Shuffled reference: 1000 circular block shuffles of the pain scores (day-to-day similarity kept), each making the same best-of-nine choice in either direction.

High vs low pain: the pain scores were split into thirds, using one score per pain report: a score of 7 or below counts as low pain, 8 or above counts as high pain, and the scores in between were left out of this comparison.
A logistic fit at each of the 22 cells matched the folded ordering in 22; a mismatch means the band carries little.

device_timing_ranges.averaging_source: Medtronic BrainSense Tip Cards (2020, FIELDPORTAL1594651482409), p. 8
device_timing_ranges.averaging_caveat: The 0-30 s range is printed in the 2020 BrainSense tip card and was confirmed on the clinician tablet's Adaptive Therapy setup screen on 2026-09-15 (0.00 ms to 30.00 s, non-overlapping averages). This participant's device has run averaging from 100 ms to 30 s and never longer.
device_timing_ranges.onset_source: Clinician tablet (A610), Adaptive Therapy setup screens, read by the PI on 2026-09-15
device_timing_ranges.onset_note: The FDA summary (P960009/S478, Table 2) prints a Dual Threshold onset range of 0 to 6 min; the clinician tablet offers 0.00 ms to 30.00 s on both timers, and neither the white paper nor the A610 manual prints a range. The platform applies the tablet's 30 s, which is what can be typed.
device_timing_ranges.onset_meaning: The onset duration does not average: it holds an averaged reading past a threshold for this long before the device acts (Dual Threshold, 0 to 30 s on the tablet). A length of signal longer than the averaging range can only be approximated as a sustained level, not as a mean, and only up to one averaging window plus one onset hold.
